To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

refrigerant performance can be enhanced by using refrigerants with high values of latent heats, liquid thermal conductivities and vapour densities, and low values of molecular weights and liquid viscosities.
the performance of a refrigerant in a system depends on the properties of the refrigerant, the system design and the operating conditions.

refrigerant selection for an air-conditioning system is a compromise between capacity and COP, and refrigerants with high latent heat and liquid thermal conductivity are desirable for high capacity and high density and low viscosity for high COP.

the effects of thermo- physical properties on refrigerant performances.
the effects of thermo- physical properties and derived parameters on the refrigerant system performance.
the development of a new refrigerant with a high COP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no refrigerant which is the best for all refrigeration applications.

the refrigerant with the lowest molecular weight, the highest latent heat, the highest vapour density, the lowest vapour specific heat and liquid viscosity and the highest liquid thermal conductivity would give the best system performance.
the refrigerants with the best performance are those that have high latent heat, liquid density, vapour thermal conductivity and low vapour viscosity, liquid viscosity and molecular weight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
refrigerant performance comparison is a complex task, which requires a detailed understanding of all the properties involved and the effect that they have on the system.
the performance of the refrigerant is dependent on the properties of refrigerant itself.
refrigerant properties have a great influence on the system performance.

the performance of the refrigerant in the system is not only dependent on its physical properties but also its interactions with the other system components, such as the oil.
the refrigerant properties should be considered in refrigerant selection and refrigerant performance comparison.
